question: One study aims to evaluate the association between exposure to nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) and myocardial infarction. To this end, NSAID exposure will be compared among patients diagnosed with myocardial infarction during the next 2 years in a cohort of patients from the Community of Madrid against NSAID exposure in a larger control group without myocardial infarction and that will be sampled from the same cohort. What kind of study is it?

options.opa: Cohort study nested in a control case.
options.opc: Case study and prospectively nested cohorts.
options.opd: Case-control study nested in a cohort.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Observational study design -> Cohort study -> Longitudinal data collection -> 90% CHAIN: Exposure to NSAIDs -> Comparison between patients with myocardial infarction and control group -> Nested case-control study -> 85% CHAIN: Evaluation of NSAID exposure -> Comparison between patients with and without myocardial infarction -> Case-control study nested in a cohort -> 90%
enhanced_information: The study described is a case-control study nested in a cohort, aiming to evaluate the association between exposure to NSAIDs and myocardial infarction. This design involves comparing NSAID exposure between patients diagnosed with myocardial infarction and a control group without myocardial infarction sampled from the same cohort.
analysis: The study described involves comparing NSAID exposure between patients diagnosed with myocardial infarction and a control group without myocardial infarction sampled from the same cohort. This design is characteristic of a case-control study nested in a cohort.
